verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless and stubborn, as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees, but says that through practice and letting go, it can be trained. The idea is that the mind resists force, yet it can be steadied by returning to it again and again, not by gripping it tighter.
verse.for_you: The terror at 2am and the rating you fear is your mind running ahead of you. You do not have to hold the wind. You can return to your breath, to the dark room, to the fact that the phone is still in your hand, and let the storm pass through.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra lists the certainties that make the wise calm.
verse.sanskrit: चिन्तया जायते दुःखं नान्यथेहेति निश्चयी । तया हीनः सुखी शान्तः सर्वत्र गलितस्पृहः ॥
verse.line: Suffering is born of worry, nothing else. Free of worry, you are happy and at peace.
verse.translation: One who knows for certain that suffering here is born of worry and nothing else is free of it, happy, at peace, and unattached everywhere.
verse.why: Most suffering is made of worry; knowing what you can't control loosens it.
verse.misuse: Real problems still need attention; this is about the extra pain rumination adds.

prasang.title: The certainties of the calm
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra lists convictions that make a person calm: things arise and pass by nature, fortune and misfortune come in their time, and suffering is born of worry alone.
prasang.lesson: Most suffering is made of worry; knowing what you can't control loosens it.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, who sits surrounded by wealth and power yet cannot sleep. He tells him that the only thing that ever creates pain is the mind's habit of worrying. When a person sees clearly that worry itself is the root of all trouble, the grip of fear loosens. The real problems are still there, but the extra agony of imagining them over and over falls away. The mind can then rest in the present, even when the future is uncertain.
verse.for_you: The rating on your work is a real thing. But the terror you feel at two in the morning is mostly the extra weight of worry. You can let the rating be what it is, without letting it become the story that keeps you awake.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that your only right is to the work itself, not to its fruits. He speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, where the stakes are life and death, and shows that the moment for action is now, not after the outcome is known. The verse asks you to act fully, but to stop letting the result own you. It is a steadying thought, because it names a boundary between what you can do and what you cannot, and it lets you rest in the doing.
verse.for_you: Your work is yours to do. The results are not yours to hold. You can put your full attention into the task, but the rating is not yours to hold. Let it be what it is, and let your attention rest on the doing, not the outcome.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verse.sanskrit: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verse.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
verse.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha how a person who is free inside lives in the world. They let go of what is lost, take up what comes, do the work at hand, speak gently, and treat the whole world as family. They are busy on the outside but unhurried inside. They act fully in the world without letting it agitate them. The truth is, you can do your work with a clear mind even when the ground beneath you feels shaky.
verse.for_you: Your work and your visa are real things, and you are doing them. But the terror that a bad rating will erase your life in days is not a fact. It is a story your mind is telling you over and over. You can do the work at hand while the fear is there.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna describes those whom he lifts out of the sea of mortality (12.7).

verse.translation: But those who lay all their actions in me, intent on me, and worship me meditating with single-minded yoga — for them, whose minds are set on me, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth, Partha.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna what it means to be truly devoted. He says that those who place every action in him and keep their mind fixed on him are lifted out of the cycle of life and death. verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verse.sanskrit: प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा नैव धीरस्य दुर्ग्रहः । यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत्कृत्वा तिष्ठतः सुखम् ॥
verse.line: Don't cling to doing or to not doing. Do what's in front of you and stay at ease.
verse.translation: The steady person has no stubborn attachment to doing or to not doing. Doing whatever comes to be done, he stays at ease.

prasang.title: The calm of the wise
prasang.summary: In a hundred verses Ashtavakra paints the inner peace of the wise: calm while busy, unmoved by gain or loss, praise or blame, at ease whether in the city or the forest. The restless, by contrast, chase peace and never find it.
prasang.lesson: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka about the calm of the wise. The wise person does not cling to the idea of doing things or not doing things. They simply do what is in front of them and remain at ease. The restless chase peace and never find it, but the calm person holds ordinary life without struggle. This is the end of the long chapter on peace. The calm is not found by chasing it or changing places, but by how you hold your daily work.
verse.for_you: Try one hour where you do nothing for work, and one evening where the phone stays away. Let the silence hold you instead of filling it.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

depth.life: You are terrified, and your mind is running the show at 2am. You check Slack again and again, trying to hold the terror of a bad rating in your hands like a heavy stone. But the storm you are trying to hold is not the rating. It is the fear of what might happen.
depth.points: The mind is restless, turbulent and strong. It is not your enemy, but it is not your master either. It runs ahead of you, living the future in the dark. You are trying to hold the wind, and the wind is just your own fear of what might happen.
depth.practice: When the 2am check comes, pause for three breaths before you touch the screen. Let the storm pass through without you holding it.
depth.question: What would it feel like to let the wind blow through for just one night?
